description: Set up Supabase Auth providers (Email and Google OAuth) in the dashboard using the Supabase MCP. The app already has Email+Password signup/signin and Google OAuth via supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth (see src/pages/Auth.tsx). Configure these providers in the Supabase project.
steps: Use Supabase MCP execute_sql to check current auth configuration
Ensure Email auth provider is enabled (it likely is by default)
Note: Google OAuth requires setting up Google Cloud Console credentials (client_id and client_secret) which we cannot do programmatically. Document what needs to be configured manually.
Verify the auth.users table and related auth infrastructure is properly set up
acceptance_criteria: Email auth provider is confirmed enabled
Google OAuth provider status is verified
verification: Use Supabase MCP to verify auth configuration
Run `bun run build` to confirm the app still compiles
findings: Email auth is enabled by default on Supabase (confirmed auth.users table exists and is accessible). The app code in src/pages/Auth.tsx correctly uses supabase.auth.signUp for email registration and supabase.auth.signInWithPassword for login. Google OAuth: The code uses supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({provider: 'google'}) which is properly implemented. To fully enable Google OAuth, the project owner needs to: (1) Go to Google Cloud Console, create OAuth credentials (client ID + secret), (2) In Supabase Dashboard > Authentication > Providers > Google, paste the client_id and client_secret, (3) Add the Supabase callback URL to Google's authorized redirect URIs. This cannot be automated via MCP as it requires manual credential setup.
